title: Senior Production Editor
description:
We are looking for a Senior Production Editor for Macmillan Adult Trade. This role will production-edit approximately 35 to 40 books a year, or 15 to 25 books at a time. They will manage the production editorial process from assessing manuscripts for copyediting needs to hiring and managing freelancers to proofreading and indexing page proofs as well as checking all stages of text, photo inserts, and jackets/covers throughout the bookmaking process. They will be responsible for quality control and compliance with departmental procedures. Proficiency with digital copyediting and routing required as well as knowledge of workflow systems.
What You'll Do:

• Handling production editorial work for original fiction and nonfiction titles from manuscript to bound book, as well as paperback conversions.

• Electronic styling of manuscripts for design and composition.

• Hiring freelance copyeditors, proofreaders, and indexers, and reviewing their work through all passes.

• Cleaning and preparing copyedited, author-reviewed manuscripts for design and typesetting.

• Collating changes from authors and freelancers in page proofs and resolving queries ahead of transmittal.

• Copyediting jacket/cover copy and ancillary marketing material, including sales quotes, reading group guides, bound galley cover copy, and proofreading jackets/covers, insert captions, and additional material.

• Frequent and ongoing collaboration with Production, Design, and Editorial departments as needed concerning scheduling; editorial revisions suggested by authors, copyeditors, or proofreaders; complying with Legal department directives.

• Updating progress of projects in various digital tracking systems, using correct file-naming conventions and adhering to documented best practices.

• Providing task- and project-specific support for other production editors to ensure that coverage is maintained during planned vacation and discretionary days.

What You'll Bring:

• Extensive background in adult trade fiction and nonfiction

• Ability to work independently as well as part of a team, anticipating problems, troubleshooting solutions, and prioritizing

• Strong working knowledge of grammar and punctuation, including expertise with the Chicago Manual of Style, with an aptitude for enforcing style rules while also respecting author voice

• Meticulous attention to detail; work well under pressure; good oral and verbal communication

• Ability to meet deadlines while juggling multiple projects at once

• Work well with others in a tactful manner, displaying common sense and initiative.

• Seven to ten years’ experience as a production editor, preferably in adult trade fiction/nonfiction

• Copyediting and proofreading at a high level

• Technical proficiency in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat (including comfort with PDF markup tools), and Workflow/Metadata systems

• Bachelor’s degree or commensurate experience

The salary range for this role is $70,000 - $75,000.
Macmillan Publishers is the U.S. trade company that is part of the Holtzbrinck Publishing Group, a large family-owned group of media companies headquartered in Stuttgart, Germany. Holtzbrinck Publishing Group's publishing companies include prominent imprints around the world that publish a broad range of award-winning books for children and adults in all categories and formats.
U.S. publishers include Celadon Books, Farrar, Straus and Giroux, Flatiron Books, Henry Holt & Company, Macmillan Audio, Macmillan Children’s Publishing Group, The St. Martin's Publishing Group, and Tor Publishing Group. In the UK, Australia, India, and South Africa, companies in the Holtzbrinck Publishing Group publish under the Pan Macmillan name. The German publishing company, Holtzbrinck Deutsche Buchverlage, includes among its imprints S. Fischer, Kiepenheuer & Witsch, Rowohlt, and Droemer Knaur.

title: Manufacturing Test Engineer II (Onsite)
description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As a Manufacturing Test Engineer, you’ll play a critical role in ensuring the quality and performance of the devices that help save lives and keep communities safer. You’ll develop and support advanced automated test systems used in the production of our cutting-edge body-worn cameras, smart weapons, and other connected devices. Your work will directly impact our ability to scale with quality, reliability, and speed.

What You’ll Do

Location: Onsite
Reports to: Manufacturing Engineering Manager, Video
Direct Reports: N/A

• Design, develop, and maintain robust automated test systems for Axon’s manufacturing lines, leveraging LabVIEW and TestStand

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams-hardware, firmware, software, and manufacturing-to define test strategies and implement scalable solutions

• Drive continuous improvement in test coverage, reliability, and efficiency to meet Axon’s quality and throughput goals

• Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by developing and deploying test systems that scale from prototype to mass production

• Troubleshoot complex test issues and perform root cause analysis on hardware and system-level failures

• Generate detailed test documentation and support the training of technicians and operators

• Create Statements of Work (SOW) and other technical specifications for third party integrators.

• Analyze test data, generate reports, and provide feedback to engineering and quality teams.

• Ensure compliance with safety and quality standards in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

What You Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

• 2+ years of experience in a test engineering role, ideally within an electronics manufacturing environment

• Strong proficiency in LabVIEW and TestStand (NI certifications like CLAD, CLD are a plus)

• Experience with instrumentation and hardware interfaces (e.g., I2C, UART, SPI, GPIB, USB, Ethernet)

• Solid understanding of manufacturing test methods for digital and analog electronics

• Passion for Axon’s mission and a commitment to working on impactful, real-world products

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

• Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

• And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Harness Engineer, Director
description:

The Opportunity
As a Director, AI Harness Engineering, you will lead a new internal team that lets AI coding agents do reliable work at scale. As agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness), and we're building a dedicated Harness Engineering team to own it. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will design and build harness components while leading and growing a regional team of harness engineers and setting the quality bar for AI-assisted engineering across the organization.

What You’ll Contribute

• Help design, build, and evolve the harness, the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role; you will contribute to the development, not just direct it.

• Build and maintain feedforward guides (agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods) that help agents get it right the first time and drive their adoption across teams.

• Build feedback sensors, custom linters, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers.

• Own AI governance for your region: define authority boundaries for what agents may merge unaided, establish LLM testing infrastructure, and ensure AI-generated output meets quality, safety, and compliance thresholds before release.

• Define and own cross-organizational QA and quality-gating standards, ensuring consistent, enforceable engineering practices across teams and product areas.

• Run the steering loop at scale when agents repeat a class of mistake, ensure a control is engineered so it cannot happen again - and treat repository knowledge (docs, specs, context) as the system of record, fighting drift continuously.

• Decide where each control runs in the path to production, fast checks pre-commit, moreexpensive checks post-integration, and continuous sensors that scan for drift outside the changelifecycle - keeping quality as far left as is economical.

• Establish observability into agent work and own the measures that matter - cost per merged PR,time-to-merge for agent-assisted PRs, review velocity relative to PR size, defect escape rate, andagent-PR survival rate - using them to direct where the team invests next.

• Manage, coach, and grow a geographically distributed team of harness engineers; partner withstakeholders to attract talent, set goals, and measure and reward performance.

• Work closely with other engineering leaders and product management to turn specifications and acceptance criteria into enforceable controls, and to align the harness with platform and delivery roadmaps.

• Demonstrate expertise through internal enablement, presentations, and thought leadership on agent-augmented engineering.

What We’re Seeking

• Strong software engineering background with experience in large, complex codebases, and genuine care for architecture, testing, and maintainability - you remain hands-on.

• Strong consensus building skills.

• Hands-on experience with AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, or similar) and a well-developed feel for where they succeed and fail.

• Experience building engineering tooling across a modern stack, linters and static analysis, CI/CD pipelines, containerized build/test enviro

Description
TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We’ve been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners - people with no prior tech background - through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. As a Technical Owner you’ll own every technical decision behind our programs, from the first conversation with a course author to the bug that never reaches a learner. The role is fully remote and full-time, for candidates based outside the US.
What you will do

•
Own each program’s technical setup. Know its environments, services, providers, and autotests, and keep a written map of what each program depends on.

•
Shape new and updated programs. Collect requirements from authors and constraints from product, test the options, and land on a workable trade-off.

•
Replace what no longer fits. Find, cost, and run the switch when a tool, provider, or setup is outdated or too expensive.

•
Manage providers. Compare offers, negotiate terms, and own integrations with external providers.

•
Lead autotest coverage. Set coverage and priorities for the autotest engineer, and write or fix tests yourself when needed.

•
Be our customer to engineering. Write specs with acceptance criteria for automation, API, and platform needs, and chase each one to done.

•
Cut bugs reaching learners. Trace each bug to where it entered, close the gap with a test, check, or process change, and track the trend.

•
End-to-end technical ownership. 3+ years in engineering, QA automation, or technical operations, including choosing a product’s setup and living with the trade-off after launch.

Solid mid-level coding. Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, Git, CI, containers, and REST APIs: enough to read unfamiliar code, fix bugs, and write autotests.

•
English for requirements work. Strong enough to run requirements sessions and write specs engineering teams accept without a round of questions.

Nice to have

•
Leading engineers. Leading or mentoring at least one engineer, ideally in test automation.

•
EdTech and content validation. LMS or autograded courses, QA or release work, or agents that check content for accuracy and freshness.

•
Automation and data stack. Claude Code, MCP, n8n or Make; SQL and dashboards.

What we can offer you

•
Ownership. Real decision-making power in your area: we trust your expertise and don’t micromanage.

•
Remote and flexible. Fully remote collaboration

•
Digital office. Slack, Notion, Miro, and Zoom, with every license you need.

We don’t wait for the market to tell us what’s next. We build it.

The Role

The Executive Creative Director is Oxford Road 's most senior creative leader, accountable for the quality, performance, and culture of everything the Creative department produces across host-read, pre-produced audio, and bespoke 360-degree campaigns. This role owns the creative standard across every client account, not just the highest-profile ones, and is responsible for ensuring that standard is consistently met, measurably tied to results, and strengthened by every test the team runs.

This is a leadership role built around three commitments: quality on everything that ships, creative tied to performance, and testing built in as a standard practice rather than an afterthought. The ECD is the keeper of the craft and the driver of the creative department's contribution to client outcomes, agency growth, and new business.

Scope of Ownership

• Owns creative quality end-to-end across all client accounts: reviewing work in flight before it ships, closing the feedback loop to writers directly, and maintaining a consistent standard across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns how Audiolytics is used across the department: as a benchmark and coaching tool integrated with compliance and performance data, not as a checkbox exercise

• Owns the talent onboarding, briefing, and feedback process: ensuring every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time

• Owns the connection between creative output and market performance: working with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines and translate results into creative direction

• Owns a test-and-learn culture in partnership with Analytics: bringing creative hypotheses, making testing a standard part of how briefs are written, and ensuring what the team learns shapes the next round of work

• Owns the full creative team: leading and developing writers across Bespoke and Format tiers and producers across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns key client and talent relationships at the senior creative level: these relationships stay direct, not delegated

• Owns the department's presence in new business pitches: concept development, pitch decks, and demo work, including a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles)

• Owns creative support for bespoke, creator-first partnerships and 360-degree campaigns

• Does not own test design, statistical analysis, or tracking infrastructure; those sit within Analytics

• Does not own production cost, change-order pricing, or P those sit within Finance

description:
Company description
 
Service Measure (SM) is a field data collection company founded in 2013 in New York. 
 
We collect data where automation is not possible. We count features, take pictures, make videos, record speech, and scan areas for every detail you need to make more informed decisions. Our field data collection teams are spread across Europe and North America, ready to accept new challenges.
 
Project objective
 
The goal of the project is to help collect images of streets, main points of interest and public areas in the USA. title: Hydrus - Voice Contributor - English (British)

About the Project 
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. We're looking for native-level speakers who can deliver natural, everyday-sounding speech - recordings that hold up whether you're reading a script or speaking spontaneously. 
Please note: the recordings you produce may be used to create synthesized, AI-generated voices for conversational AI products. Full details on how your data is collected, used, shared, and retained are set out in a Consent Form, which you'll review and sign before any paid session recording begins. 
 
What You'll Do If Selected: 
Two supervised sessions of approximately 4 hours each, guided in real time by a Session Director on a separate recording platform. 
Record scripted material in a natural, conversational tone - faithfully, without a polished, performed, or “announcer” delivery. 
Record unscripted, spontaneous speech on a given topic, matching the same warmth and pace as your scripted takes. 
Set up and manage your own recording space and equipment for session recording. 
Deliver all recordings entirely in the required language (with specific dialect), without code-switching into other languages or dialects. 
 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
Experience as a voice actor, actor, or theater performer, or a comparable performance background. 
Native or native-equivalent fluency in the required language (with specific dialect). 
Access to a quiet recording space, free of echo and background noise (acoustically treated for session recording, if selected). 
Owns or will acquire a dedicated, professional-grade microphone for the audition (e.g. RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti), upgrading to a qualifying USB condenser or XLR mic + audio interface for session recording if selected. Built-in laptop mics, AirPods, earbuds, and headsets are not accepted at any stage. 
Owns closed-back monitoring headphones (required for session recording if selected). 
Comfortable both self-directing for the audition and taking live direction from a Session Director in guided sessions. 
 
Preferred (nice to have, not required) 
Professional voice-over experience (dubbing/ADR, audiobook, podcasting) in a conversational rather than commercial/announcer register. 
Baseline audio hygiene: comfortable setting mic distance and catching noise, clipping, or distortion yourself. 
An existing home recording setup already treated for sound. 
 
Your Data & Privacy 
Before any session recording, you'll be asked to review and sign a Consent Form covering how your voice recordings are collected, used (including to train synthesized/AI voice models), shared with approved partners, retained, and how to exercise your data rights (access, correction, deletion, and more, depending on where you live). If you'd like to review these terms before applying, contact us and we'll share a copy in advance.

title: AI & Innovation Lead, G&A

description:
At Sanity https://sanity.io/, we’re building the future of AI-powered Content Operations. Our AI Content Operating System gives teams the freedom to model, create, and automate content the way their business works, accelerating digital development and supercharging content operations efficiency. This role sits at the intersection of G&A operations, data, workflow automation, and AI. You bring the domain depth: you know how G&A teams actually work, where their processes and systems break, and which manual work eats their week. You’ll start with Finance, then quickly extend into People and the rest of G&A. You’ll prototype the fix yourself, vibe-coding agents, apps, and workflows on Sanity’s own platform and AI tools. Systems Engineering and the Data team back you on architecture, security, and production hardening, so your ideas become systems the business can rely on. If you’re a G&A operator who has already started rebuilding your own work with AI, and you want to do that for an entire G&A organization, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU WOULD DO:

- Shape and execute on the AI first transformation roadmap for G&A: map where G&A teams lose time, and decide what to build, buy, or automate first.

- Run intake, prioritization and stage-gates for the G&A transformation portfolio, with clear owners, decision rights and a regular exec review cadence

- Prototype agents, apps, and automations yourself on Sanity’s platform and AI tools, then partner with Systems Engineering to take the ones that work to production.

- Translate G&A processes into clear specs and prototypes for engineering: data flows, system of record, controls, edge cases, and what “done” looks like.

- Build for trust through controls, audit trails, access management, data quality, and human-in-the-loop review, so G&A teams and auditors can rely on what you ship.

- Partner with the Data and IT teams on the G&A systems and data infrastructure, connecting the systems G&A and our data warehouse together.

- Drive adoption across G&A: train teams, document the paved paths, and help each function run more of its own work with AI and retire legacy manual processes.

- Measure impact through hours saved, cycle times, error and exception rates, adoption, AI evals, and stakeholder feedback.

- Help shape the practices and culture of a young Systems Engineering team with a strong bias toward practical impact.

ABOUT YOU:

- Remote in North America (SF preferred).

- Deep G&A domain knowledge, ideally 8+ years in Finance, Accounting, People ops, or business operations at a software company.

- Hands-on experience applying AI to G&A work, for example leading an AI program for your function, automating a core process, or building agents for your own team.

- Comfortable building prototypes with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar). You don’t need to be a software engineer, and you’re not afraid of a terminal.

- Understands APIs, data flows, and how G&A systems connect: what moves between the ERP, HRIS, CRM, contract tools, and warehouse, and where it breaks.

- Excited by AI as an operating model, including agents, tool use, structured context, prompts, evals, and automation.

- Cares deeply about controls, accuracy, auditability, and systems G&A teams can confidently rely on.

- Program management strength: you can run a cross-functional roadmap, align stakeholders, and land change with teams that are busy running the business.

- Comfortable with ambiguity and able to turn loosely defined business problems into shipped solutions.

- Clear communicator who can explain G&A processes to engineers and technical tradeoffs to G&A teams.

title: Product Support Specialist
description:
ABOUT CARTESIA

Our mission is to architect AI that learns from and interacts with the world like humans do.

We're pioneering the model architectures that will make this possible. Our founding team met as PhDs at the Stanford AI Lab, where we invented State Space Models or SSMs, a new primitive for training efficient, large-scale foundation models. Our team combines deep expertise in model innovation and systems engineering paired with a design-minded product engineering team to build and ship cutting edge models and experiences.

We're funded by leading investors at Index Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, along with Factory, Conviction, A Star, General Catalyst, SV Angel, Databricks and others. We're fortunate to have the support of many amazing advisors, and 90+ angels across many industries, including the world's foremost experts in AI.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Cartesia builds real-time voice and audio AI, and our customers put our models in front of their own users every day. As our Product Support Specialist, you’ll own the front line, the first person customers hear from when something is unclear, broken, or blocking them. You’re obsessed with the customer experience: you dig into every problem, don’t let go until the customer is unblocked, and treat each ticket as a chance to make Cartesia better. Our support function is still taking shape, so you’ll help shape the processes that define our post-sales support and set the standard for how customers experience Cartesia. This role is based in San Francisco.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Own the support queue across Slack, Pylon, WhatsApp, and email, with extra attention to priority and enterprise accounts.

- Keep response and resolution times within SLA, so customers always know where their issue stands.

- Resolve L1 and L2 issues independently across billing, documentation, configuration, APIs, and voices.

- Troubleshoot complex L3 issues, reproduce them, gather the relevant details, and escalate to On-Call with complete context.

- Partner with Engineering and Product to turn customer issues into fixes by, writing clear bug reports and creating actionable Linear tickets, and pushing them to get prioritized when customers are blocked

- Reduce repeat tickets by building internal runbooks, improving our customer-facing documentation, and sharing what you learn about troubleshooting

- Help with incident communications by coordinating customer updates, explaining impact, and keeping customers informed on progress until resolution.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- 2+ years in technical support for an API or developer product, working a live queue of customers who write code.

- Hands-on troubleshooting skills: you can read requests, responses, and logs, reproduce an issue, and tell a bug from a configuration problem.

- Clear written communication, both to customers and in bug reports, runbooks, and docs.

- Experience supporting customers in real-time channels like shared Slack channels or chat, and balancing speed with accuracy.

- A track record of working with engineers to get issues fixed, including filing well-formed tickets in a tracker like Linear.

- Comfort with ambiguity: you make good calls without a playbook, and when one is missing, you write it.

BONUS

- Experience supporting an API or developer product, where your customers write code.

- Familiarity with AI products, especially voice, speech, or audio products such as text-to-speech, speech recognition, or voice agents.

- Experience writing customer-facing updates during an incident or outage.

Note: Cartesia participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with Form I-9 information to confirm employment eligibility after hire.

MORE DETAILS

🏢 In-office policy: We’re an in-person team based out of offices in 🇺🇸 San Francisco, 🇬🇧 London and 🇮🇳 Bangalore. We love being in the office, hanging out together, and learning from each other every day.

Maps launches its private beta today.

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like - and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds - which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia - many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact - this is the place.

ABOUT THE ROLE AND YOU

We're hiring a Demand Generation Lead to own pipeline generation for North America. Today, demand gen at Lorikeet is spread across several people who each carry a piece of it alongside their day jobs - this role exists to change that. You'll be the first person whose sole focus is building the machine that fills our pipeline.

You'll own a North American pipeline target and work backwards from it - designing and executing the mix of events, webinars, industry programs, and campaigns that gets us there. You'll also help shape how demand gen scales as a function as we grow, defining the playbook rather than inheriting one. This is a mid-senior role for someone who's comfortable being accountable to a hard revenue-linked number with a high degree of autonomy over how they hit it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Partner closely with Sales to ensure every program converts - tight handoffs, fast follow-up, and shared accountability for pipeline quality

- Build the demand gen operating infrastructure from scratch: campaign tracking, attribution, and reporting that give us a real view of the funnel

- Identify which channels and plays are worth scaling and which to kill, iterating quickly with limited resources

- Define the demand gen playbook for Lorikeet as we grow, laying the foundation for the function's future team and budget

THE RIGHT CANDIDATE

We're looking for someone who is energized by owning a number, not just running programs - someone who sees a pipeline target as a puzzle to reverse-engineer rather than a burden. The ideal candidate learned the fundamentals of demand gen inside a rigorous, well-resourced marketing org, then proved they could build the whole thing from scratch with none of that scaffolding.

You might be a fit if you:

- Have 4-7 years of demand generation experience in B2B SaaS

- Have early-stage startup (under ~100 people) experience, building the demand gen function from zero - choosing channels, setting up systems, and owning outcomes without a big team or budget

- Have hands-on experience across the program mix: field events, webinars, executive dinners, and industry programs, not just digital campaigns

- Think in pipeline, not MQLs - you work backwards from revenue targets and can defend your math

- Operate with high autonomy and low need for direction, and are relentless about follow-through

title: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting
description: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting About this role We are looking for a Prevention Analyst - Pentester, to join our Prevention track. An attacker does not look at one server in isolation. They look at everything a company exposes to the internet and work out where to start. You will do the same for our clients, taking the attacker’s view of their external attack surface, seeing what an attacker sees, and doing what an attacker would do next. That means reading the story behind an attack surface. A forgotten subdomain, an old login portal, and a misconfigured mail server may each look minor on their own. Together they can show how an organisation has grown, where its blind spots are, and where someone could get in. When you find a potential weak point, you dig into it technically to find out how far an attacker could actually go. This is not a classic penetration testing role. The deep dive draws on pentest methodology and expertise, but it is not a full pentest, and you will not spend your weeks writing long reports. We focus on finding the high impact vulnerabilities that need attention now and getting them to the client in a form they can act on. This is for someone with hands on pentesting experience who wants to work across many customer environments, sharpen their attacker mindset, and grow into owning complex prevention engagements end to end. What you will do Assess clients’ external attack surface as a whole, from the attacker’s perspective. Identify gaps and weaknesses across the surface, not just within a single asset, and work out how they connect.<

title: Financial Planning Analyst
description:
Job Title: Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist
Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. client business hours
About the Role:
Our client is seeking a Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist to build financial models, manage planning cycles, and provide forward-looking insights that guide strategy. This role requires strong analytical skills, mastery of modeling tools, and the ability to translate numbers into actionable recommendations. You will work closely with finance leaders and department heads to ensure budgets and forecasts are accurate, realistic, and strategically aligned.
Responsibilities :
Budget Development:

• Lead preparation of annual operating and capital budgets.

• Consolidate inputs across departments and business units.

• Ensure budgets align with company goals and resource constraints.

Forecasting:

• Maintain rolling forecasts for revenue, expenses, and cash flow.

• Update models monthly or quarterly with actuals, adjusting assumptions.

• Build scenario and sensitivity analyses to test potential outcomes.

Variance Analysis:

• Compare actual results to budgets/forecasts.

• Prepare written commentary to explain variances and recommend corrective actions.

Financial Modeling:

• Build dynamic Excel or Google Sheets models (DCF, ROI, IRR, break-even).

• Use advanced formulas, macros, or BI tool integrations to improve accuracy.

Reporting:

• Prepare management reporting packages with dashboards and visualizations.

• Present insights to executives, highlighting risks and opportunities.

Collaboration:

• Partner with department heads to align forecasts with operational plans.

• Work with FP&A teams to refine planning assumptions.

Process Improvement:

• Identify inefficiencies in forecasting workflows.

• Implement new FP&A software or improve data integrations (Adaptive Insights, Anaplan, Workday, or equivalent).

What Makes You a Perfect Fit:

• Highly analytical with an eye for detail.

• Comfortable building models from scratch and explaining them simply.

• Proactive in identifying trends, risks, and opportunities.

• Skilled communicator who can influence leaders through data-driven storytelling.

Required Experience & Skills (Minimum):

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.

• 3+ years in financial planning/analysis, budgeting, or forecasting.

• Advanced Excel/Google Sheets (nested formulas, pivot tables, sensitivity modeling).

• Experience preparing variance analyses for leadership.

Ideal Experience & Skills:

• FP&A tool experience (Anaplan, Adaptive Insights, Hyperion, Workday).

• MBA, CFA, or CPA credential.

• Experience forecasting for SaaS, real estate, or professional services.

• Familiarity with BI/analytics platforms (Power BI, Tableau, Looker).

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?
A Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist’s day revolves around building clarity about the future of the business. You will:

• Maintain financial models - updating them with actuals and revising assumptions based on market or internal trends.

• Analyze variances - reviewing how actual results differ from plan and preparing written explanations with supporting data.

• Support decision-making - running scenario analyses (“what happens if revenue grows 15%?” “what if headcount increases by 20?”) and presenting implications to leadership.

• Collaborate across teams - meeting with department managers to validate budget assumptions and ensure spending aligns with strategy.

• Deliver reporting - packaging forecasts and analyses into dashboards and executive-ready presentations.

• Continuously improve - refining models, implementing forecasting software, and streamlining inputs to shorten cycles.

In essence: the role is about ensuring the organization has reliable forward-looking data to guide strategy, supported by strong financial models and clear commentary.
Key Metrics for Success (KPIs):

• Forecast accuracy within ±5-10%.

• Budget completion within agreed timelines

Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we're helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.

We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.

500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com

title: Strategic Component Manager – Inventory & Supply Optimisation
description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being-on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

The Strategic Component Manager advances Ciena ’s supply-chain and working-capital objectives by optimizing component inventory across the enterprise. This role monetizes excess inventory, identifies strategic purchasing opportunities that strengthen supply assurance and reduce component costs, and develops financially supported recommendations for significant inventory transactions.

How you will make an impact:

• Develop and execute strategies to sell excess and surplus component inventory across Ciena ’s supply chain.

• Evaluate inventory for disposition based on excess position, demand outlook, component lifecycle, market conditions, and potential financial recovery.

• Build qualified disposition channels through authorized distributors, brokers, suppliers, contract manufacturers, and secondary-market opportunities; solicit, evaluate, and negotiate offers.

• Coordinate approved inventory sales with appropriate commercial controls, documentation, financial visibility, pipeline management, and reporting on value recovered.

• Identify strategic component purchases based on supply availability, lead times, lifecycle events, market conditions, demand requirements, inventory exposure, and financial return.

• Execute commercially justified strategic buys, bridge buys, and opportunistic purchases that improve supply continuity or deliver measurable material cost reductions.

• Partner with Finance, Inventory Management, Global Commodity Management, and supply-chain leadership to validate business cases, align sourcing and disposition strategies, establish governance, and present recommendations.

The must haves:

• Application of component market knowledge to evaluate inventory, pricing dynamics, lifecycle events, supplier constraints, and supply-chain risk.

• Application of commercial judgment to negotiate pricing, terms, offers, and inventory arrangements with approved market participants.

• Application of financial acumen to quantify recovery, inventory valuation, cost reduction, working-capital impact, inventory exposure, and financial return.

• Execution capability to manage inventory transactions, controls, documentation, reporting, and cross-functional governance.

Pay Range:
The annual pay range for this position in Canada is C$74,200 - C$118,000.
Pay ranges at Ciena are designed to accommodate variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions, and locations, reflecting our diverse products, industries, and lines of business. Please note that the pay range information provided in this posting pertains specifically to the primary location, which is the top location listed in case multiple locations are available.
Non-Sales employees may be eligible for a discretionary incentive bonus, while Sales employees may be eligible for a sales commission. In addition to competitive compensation, Ciena offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, participation in 401(K) (USA) & DCPP (Canada) with company matching, Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company-paid holidays, paid sick leave, and vacation time. We also comply with all applicable laws regarding Paid Family Leave and other leaves of absence.

The Cyber Security Analyst serves as an advanced escalation point and the 'front door' for complex security incidents, advanced queries, and unhandled items not resolved by the MSSP SOC.

Additionally, the analyst is responsible for performing in-depth security incident investigations, proactive threat hunting, threat intelligence analysis, and offering expert technical guidance across all Ocado functions.

• Act as the primary internal escalation point and 'front door' for security incidents, complex queries, and unhandled alerts or items not resolved by the MSSP SOC.

title: Growth Lead
description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. At SentinelOne , we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne , your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

title: Product Marketing Manager

About the Company:

ArcSite is the leading mobile sketching and drawing-based takeoff and estimating solution, trusted by designers, field sales teams, technicians, and inspectors. Our intuitive platform empowers users to create professional drawings on any device-without the steep learning curve of traditional CAD software-helping businesses save time, generate quotes faster, and close deals more efficiently.
We’re a remote-first team with a strong sense of community, driven by growth, collaboration, and our core values: start with the customer, constantly improve, take risks, operate with transparency, and own it. At ArcSite , every team member has the opportunity to grow their career while making an impact, shaping the future of design, and living these values in everything we do.
About the Role:
As Product Marketing Manager, you’ll help connect ArcSite ’s product, customers, and go-to-market strategy. You’ll own messaging and positioning for key product areas, lead go-to-market launches, support sales and self-serve conversion, and bring customer and market insights back to the Product and Marketing teams.
You’ll work closely with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to understand our customers and competitive landscape, translate product capabilities into compelling customer value, and ensure we bring new products and features to market effectively.
This is a hands-on role for a product marketer who is comfortable taking ownership, working cross-functionally, and turning customer and market insights into clear positioning and actionable go-to-market plans.
Key Responsibilities:

• Own messaging and positioning: Develop clear, differentiated messaging and positioning for ArcSite ’s core product, key capabilities, and new feature areas across self-serve and sales-assisted audiences.

• Lead go-to-market launches: Partner with Product, Marketing, Sales, and Engineering to plan and execute launches, including positioning, messaging, launch plans, customer communications, and success metrics.

• Build sales enablement: Create battlecards, pitch decks, FAQs, competitive materials, and other resources that help Sales effectively communicate ArcSite ’s value.

• Support self-serve and PLG growth: Develop messaging and marketing programs that help users understand ArcSite ’s value, adopt key capabilities, and move toward conversion.

• Understand our customers and buyers: Develop a strong understanding of ArcSite ’s ICPs, buyer personas, workflows, pain points, and purchasing journeys across our core contractor and specialty-trade markets.

• Conduct customer and market research: Partner with Product, Sales, and Customer Success to gather customer insights, analyze market trends, and identify opportunities to improve positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy.

• Support pricing and packaging initiatives: Partner with Product, Sales, and Marketing to evaluate pricing and packaging opportunities using existing customer, product, and market data.

• Inform product strategy: Bring customer, market, competitive, and win/loss insights to Product to help inform prioritization and product decisions.

• Enable launches and adoption: Develop beta and launch programs, messaging, and supporting materials that help customers understand and adopt new capabilities.

• Measure and optimize: Track launch performance, product adoption, conversion, and other relevant KPIs to understand what is working and continuously improve our go-to-market approach.

• Close the feedback loop: Bring insights from customers, Sales, and market research back to Product and Marketing to improve both the product and how we bring it to market.

Requirements

• 4-6+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing or a similar product-focused marketing role.

title: Electrical Engineer II, RF Test Engineer
description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As an RF Test Engineer, your work will be essential in ensuring that the wireless technologies in Axon's advanced products meet the highest performance, reliability, and compliance standards. Your hands-on expertise will drive the rigorous testing and optimization of RF systems that enable our cutting-edge body-worn cameras, vehicular systems, and connected devices. By leveraging your technical acumen and problem-solving skills, you will be instrumental in identifying and overcoming RF challenges, ensuring robust designs that operate seamlessly in diverse and demanding environments.

You will collaborate with cross-functional teams and global partners to verify and refine wireless designs, using state-of-the-art tools and methodologies. Your work will directly contribute to the development of reliable, high-performance solutions that serve Law Enforcement, Public Safety, and the communities they protect. Through your efforts, you will help deliver transformative technologies that empower public safety professionals and redefine industry standards.

What You’ll Do

• Design and implement test plans to evaluate the performance of wirelessly connected devices, ensuring they meet stringent product and regulatory requirements.

• Record RF test data and organize results, creating clear, actionable reports.

• Present findings and recommendations to cross-functional teams, enabling swift resolution of design challenges.

• Evaluate RF performance characteristics such as Total Radiated Power (TRP), Total Isotropic Sensitivity (TIS), and other over-the-air (OTA) metrics for cellular-enabled wireless devices using advanced equipment. (CMX500 and CMW500 in controlled chamber environments).

• Use instruments like spectrum analyzers and radio communication testers to assess conducted performance of wireless technologies, including LTE, 5G, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GNSS.

• Support product field evaluations to validate RF performance under diverse real-world conditions, such as urban or rural environments

• As part of a collaborative team, investigate and debug issues such as poor sensitivity, low transmit power, or signal interference in wireless devices.

• Assist in the regulatory pre-certification and formal certification test efforts for hardware by preparing test samples, working closely with external test labs, troubleshooting issues, and ensuring successful completion of certification activities.

• Expand your knowledge of RF systems, testing methodologies, and certification standards while working closely with experienced engineers to develop your technical expertise and contribute to innovative designs.

What Your Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering or similar discipline.

• Minimum of 3 years of hands-on embedded RF and wireless device testing experience

• Minimum of 3 years of wireless device test plan development for evaluating performance of various wireless interfaces against system and product requirements

• Solid understanding of basic RF principles and theory, familiar with basic RF technology circuitry stages and topologies.

• Experience characterizing RF components such as filters, switches, passives and signal paths.

title: Senior Motor Fleet Underwriter
description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Motor Fleet Underwriter, you’ll manage and grow a large portfolio of fleet business, using data and AI to assess risk and tailor cover to each client. You’ll help us move into new segments, including emerging mobility, as we build one of the UK’s largest fleet MGAs. You’ll report to our Head of Motor Underwriting.

You’ll work closely with brokers, mentor junior underwriters and help shape our products, wording and processes. AI is part of the underwriting process itself: you’ll use it to pull risk data out of submissions and triage cases faster, leaving your time for the judgement calls that need an experienced underwriter.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

- Manage and develop a large portfolio of motor fleet business and contribute strongly to team targets.

- Build strong, supportive relationships with brokers.

- Help unlock growth in new market segments, including emerging mobility.

- Collate and analyse portfolio data so our Head of Motor Underwriting can track performance.

- Improve how we gather risk information from clients, so quoting and onboarding run smoothly for clients and brokers.

- Spot where our policy wording and cover can improve, and raise it with our Head of Motor Underwriting.

- Train and develop people in the Underwriting and Operations teams, and spread underwriting knowledge across Flock.

- Use AI to extract and check risk information and speed up quoting, keeping your own judgement on every decision.

 

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

- Extensive experience underwriting motor fleet insurance.

- A track record of building strong broker relationships.

- Confidence working with data to monitor and analyse a portfolio.

- Up-to-date knowledge of the motor fleet market and the curiosity to keep up as it changes.

- Experience training or mentoring others.

- Comfortable using AI in your underwriting work, and curious about where else it can help.

Nice to have: experience with large corporate customers, ACII (qualified or working towards it), or working with product teams to get process and customer journey improvements onto the roadmap.

 

BENEFITS

- 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖

- Share Incentive Plan 📈

- Workplace Pension 💰

- Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

- Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

- Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

- £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

- £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

- 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. This role is expected to be field based rather than office based, so visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days.

title: Solution Integrations Architect - Oracle
description:
ABOUT ZIP

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement - built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.

YOUR ROLE

We’re looking for a Solution Integrations Architect to help build the technical foundation that powers Zip’s ERP and integration ecosystem. This role focuses on internal technical enablement, navigating complex customer environments to architect the cleanest possible solutions, partnering closely with Product, and driving best-in-class standards across all of Zip’s integration workflows - with a specific focus on the Oracle ecosystem.

As Zip continues to scale rapidly across enterprise customers like Coinbase, Notion, Canva, Samsara, Snowflake, and Databricks, your impact will be foundational: creating reusable integration assets, defining standards of how the Zip product interacts with external systems.

YOU WILL

You’ll work closely with our Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) teams while reporting to Engineering to design, maintain, and iterate on Zip-owned ERP and integration templates that power scalable, repeatable customer implementations. Your work will directly influence how hundreds of future implementations are delivered, raising the technical bar for both our EPD teams and our customer-facing technical consultant organization.

- Architect & standardize Oracle integrations: Design, maintain, and iterate on Zip’s core Oracle EBS and Fusion integration templates, ensuring they deliver scalable, repeatable, and robust customer implementations.

- Bridge product & the field: Work closely with Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) to ensure integration templates stay perfectly aligned with core product architecture, field insights, and emerging customer needs.

- Turn nuance into scale: Analyze complex customer implementations to identify reusable data mapping patterns and system nuances, converting bespoke solutions into standardized internal assets.

- Support pre-sales engineering: Partner with account teams during pre-sales to design and vet integration architectures, ensuring prospective customers are set up for smooth, best-practice deployments.

- Drive technical implementation excellence: Define, document, and champion technical solution consulting best practices, raising the technical bar and driving consistency across all implementations.

- Become a Multi-ERP expert: Leverage your existing Oracle EBS Fusion, P2P, and financial systems expertise to build deep fluency across additional ERP ecosystems, ultimately becoming the ultimate subject matter expert on integration architecture, data models, and Zip’s App Studio.

- Build for permanent scale: Approach every technical challenge with an engineering mindset - designing and executing a solution thoroughly once so that future implementations happen effortlessly. You balance high-level architectural design with a willingness to dive directly into API configurations and template modifications to get the job done right.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 6+ years of hands-on experience delivering integrations with Oracle EBS and Fusion environments.

- Strong foundational knowledge of core Oracle EBS/Fusion business processes, schema layouts, and
